title: AI Decision bench — nimble (local Ollama)
proves: A model that declares what it may answer is a model you can measure: the same AI Decision question runs 24 times (8 cases x 3 reps) against a local model, and the report shows whether its confidence tracks difficulty and whether the port it routed to matches the category it named.
notes:
24 serial decisions against a local model. The MODEL is not the problem: accuracy is ~1.0 on essentially every run, including the failing ones.

ITS FLAKE WAS AN ENGINE DEFECT, SINCE FOUND AND FIXED. Measured on v0.4.5 this case was wrong in ~30% of runs: either one row missing (23/24, random case) or an early exit reporting an empty report as a successful run. The cause was write visibility in fractal-core — a node's result was handed to an unbuffered channel and applied AFTER the send returned, so a successor could read the document without the write in it. A 24-iteration loop compounds a ~0.33% per-edge miss into ~30% per run. See collection/loop-write-visibility, which reproduces the same defect in 30ms, and fractal-core's writeDoc.

CONTEXT REUSE IS NOT INVOLVED — that was tested and ruled out: fresh-Context and shared-Context arms both scored 7/10, and ten consecutive runs over one Context all looped fully. `Reset state & build queue` does its job; do NOT move queue/i/results into the seed to 'fix' anything (tried, and it is a regression — it makes the flow depend on a freshly seeded Context and guarantees a skip on re-run).

CONFIRMED FIXED at this case's own operating point: 12/12 clean on the shipped image (flomorphic:latest with fractal f59b0c6), 2026-10-13. At the old ~30% rate twelve clean runs would be a 1.4% coincidence, so the `flaky` tag is dropped. repeat is 3 because each run is ~60s; three runs catch a 30% regression about two times in three, so read a single failure as a prompt to re-run rather than a verdict.
